From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>

Subject: Resale partnership: commission exceptions & deal‑registration process

Hi Jessica — great meeting last week, thanks for the time. Following up with a concise proposal so we can move toward an MOU quickly.

Summary / asks:
- Redwood is open to a standard revenue-share for reseller deals (base 70/30 split). For strategic ISV integrations where CloudPort provides bundled product + integration engineering and drives >$250k ARR in year one, we'd like to discuss a one-time commission uplift (proposed +10% to CloudPort for year one) and an expedited registration exception process.
- We also need clarity on lead registration: standard window is 60 days from first qualified discussion; exceptions are possible for named-account programs or co-sell motions.
- We've attached our latest term sheet (2026-07-28_Resale_TermSheet_v3.pdf). Can you confirm CloudPort's internal process for exceptions (who signs off, what evidence you need)?

Proposed next step: sign a short MOU so both sides can start campaign registration + align on commissions; can CloudPort review the term sheet and provide any redlines by EOD Wednesday (8/5)? If yes, I'll route to Partner Ops to draft the DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Naomi Feldman
Head of Partnerships (Americas)
Redwood Inference

Hi Naomi — thanks, pleased to continue the conversation. A few clarifying points from CloudPort's side:

1) Lead registration / exceptions:
- Our standard policy is a 90-day qualification window (we require a named AE to log the opportunity). Exceptions for "named-account" or "strategic" requests go to our Partnerships Council (monthly cadence) and require a one‑pager describing the evidence of origin (email thread, discovery notes, calendar invites).

2) Uplift for strategic integrations:
- We can consider a +10% first‑year uplift for deals where CloudPort leads the go‑to‑market and builds the integration. For enterprise deals >$500k ARR we typically escalate to Commercial Ops for an additional uplift approval.

3) Overlap and sourcing evidence:
- If CloudPort has an overlapping opportunity in your CRM (we're seeing a couple of accounts in your public pipeline), we'll need source attribution. Our legal team (cc'd: andrew.lee@cloudport.com) will also want to review exclusivity language.

I'll send redlines on clause 3.2 (lead exclusivity/registration) and propose a quick legal sync. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a short grace period (30 days) for co-sourced deals where CloudPort brings integration resources?

Regards,
Jessica
Director, Strategic Partnerships
CloudPort Inc.
jessica@cloudport.com | +1 415 777 3002
